parameters.content:
## Newsletter Subscribe + Release Notification

### What this template does
1. Accepts newsletter signups from a public form/webhook.
2. Stores each email once in an n8n Data Table.
3. Sends a welcome email to new subscribers.
4. Generates release announcement email content from release notes.
5. Sends the release email to subscribers only after an explicit send confirmation.

### Main safety rule
Release emails are blocked unless `SEND_EMAIL` is exactly `YES`. Keep it as `NO` while setting up or testing.


### Required setup before activating

- Create or select a Data Table for subscribers and replace every `REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_NEWSLETTER_DATA_TABLE_ID` placeholder.
- Configure Header Auth on both webhook triggers.
- Configure SMTP credentials on both email nodes.
- Replace `newsletter@example.com`, product names, website links, release links, and footer/legal copy.
- Point `Fetch Repo README From GitHub` to your real README or changelog source.
- Add unsubscribe/legal handling before using this with a public mailing list.

## Flow A — subscription signup

### Trigger
`When Newsletter Subscription Received` expects a POST request with an `email` field.

### Processing
The workflow normalizes the address, validates the email format, looks up the subscriber in the Data Table, then branches:
- **New email** → insert row → build welcome email → send welcome email → success response.
- **Existing email** → no duplicate insert → already-subscribed response.
- **Invalid email** → immediate 400 response.

### Data Table requirement
The subscriber table must have at least an `email` column. Keep `Lookup Subscriber by Email` set to Always Output Data so new subscribers can continue through the flow.

## Flow B — release send input

### Two ways to start
- `When Release Notification Posted` for webhook-based release announcements.
- `When Manually Started` for manual sending from the editor.

Both paths are normalized into the same fields: release version(s), optional changelog text, and `SEND_EMAIL`.

### Guardrail
`Validate Release Send Parameters` stops the workflow before subscriber lookup if:
- no semantic version is provided; or
- `SEND_EMAIL` is not exactly `YES`.

This protects the template from accidental bulk sends during setup.

## Flow B — build release email content

`Fetch Repo README From GitHub` loads release notes, then `Parse Release Versions From README` extracts the requested version sections.

The AI copywriter path creates polished release copy when enabled and correctly configured. The fallback path still builds a usable email from parsed changelog data, so the template can run without depending entirely on AI output.

Both paths converge at `Assemble Email Content`, which provides the subject and HTML used by the delivery loop.

## Flow B — send to subscribers

After content is ready, `List All Subscribers` loads the recipient list and `Loop Over Subscribers Batch 10` processes recipients one at a time.

`Send Release Announcement Email` sends the prepared HTML email. `Wait for 1 Second` throttles delivery between recipients.

Completion routing depends on how the workflow was started:
- Webhook runs return `Respond With Notification Accepted`.
- Manual runs end at `Mark Manual Send Complete`.

nodes.name: When Newsletter Subscription Received
nodes.notes: Public subscription endpoint. POST an email address to /webhook/newsletter-subscribe. Configure Header Auth before production use.

nodes.name: Lookup Subscriber by Email
nodes.notes: Checks the subscriber Data Table for the normalized email. Always Output Data must remain enabled so new subscribers continue through the flow.

nodes.name: Insert New Subscriber
nodes.notes: Stores a new subscriber. Replace the Data Table placeholder before activating the workflow.

parameters.jsCode:
const meta = $('Set Email And Subscribed At').first().json; const html = `

Welcome to Your Product updates

Thanks for subscribing. You will receive concise emails when important product releases are published.

Before using this template, replace this copy with your product name, support links, unsubscribe language, and any legal footer your audience requires.

You are receiving this email because you subscribed to product updates.

`; return [{ json: { email: meta.email, subject: 'Welcome to Your Product updates', html } }];

parameters.responseBody: ={{ { "success": true, "message": "You were already subscribed; no new email was sent" } }}

nodes.name: When Release Notification Posted
nodes.notes: Production release endpoint. Requires version and SEND_EMAIL=YES. Optional changelog text can override matching README sections.

nodes.name: Set Manual Release Parameters
nodes.notes: Manual production path. Enter one or more semantic versions and set SEND_EMAIL to YES only when you intentionally want to email the subscriber list.

nodes.name: Fetch Repo README From GitHub
nodes.notes: Replace the example raw GitHub URL with the README or changelog used as your release source.

nodes.name: Parse Release Versions From README
nodes.notes: Extracts only requested release sections, supports multiple versions, prioritizes manually supplied changelog content, and prepares user-facing highlights.

nodes.name: Release Email Copywriter Agent
nodes.notes: Optional AI editorial path. Produces structured English release copy. Errors continue to the deterministic fallback branch.

options.systemMessage:
=You are the official copywriter for "Your Product", the product configured for this workflow.

ABSOLUTE LANGUAGE RULE:
- Write ONLY in English.
- Never use Italian words, Italian sentences, or Italian UI labels in the email content.
- If the changelog or developer note contains Italian, translate it to natural English before using it.

EDITORIAL RULES — ANTI AI-SLOP:
- The email must focus only on real, user-visible changes: new features, visible behavior changes, important bug fixes, privacy/permission changes, or documentation that materially changes what users understand.
- Do not make internal maintenance sound like a feature. Ignore version bumps, dependency updates, refactors, linting, CI, build chores, formatting, and generic docs polish unless they directly affect users.
- Use the Editorial brief as the main source and priority order. Use the raw changelog only to fact-check.
- If there are no meaningful user-visible changes, write honestly that this is a small maintenance update; do not invent benefits.

FORBIDDEN GENERIC PHRASES:
- Do not write: "latest improvements", "enhanced experience", "seamless", "powerful", "various fixes", "better performance", "improved reliability", "new version is available", "full changelog", or "complete release notes" unless immediately followed by a concrete sourced detail.
- Do not use marketing filler. Every highlight needs a specific changed thing and why it matters.

CONTEXT:
- You are writing the email subscribers receive when one or more versions are announced together.
- Current label: {{ $json.version_label || $json.version }}.
- If multiple versions are included, write one aggregated update, not separate mini-emails.

FACT-CHECKING RULES:
- Every sentence must be directly supported by the editorial brief, changelog, README context, or developer note.
- Do not add setup, pricing, paid-plan, unlimited sync, future guarantees, or convenience claims unless the source explicitly says them.
- Prefer precise, modest wording over marketing claims.

STYLE RULES:
- Tone: friendly, clear, and useful. Never corporate, never hype.
- Explain important changes from the user's point of view: what changed, why it matters, and whether the user needs to do anything.
- Maximum 5 highlights, ordered by user value across all included versions.
- Each highlight must be self-contained and specific.
- Do not mention reviews, welcome text, or subscription: this email is only for existing subscribers and only about the release update.

OUTPUT:
Return ONLY the requested structured schema (subject, intro, highlights, closing). No extra text outside the schema.

nodes.name: Parse AI Structured Output
nodes.notes: Auto-fix is enabled: if the model output does not match the schema, the node asks the model for one automatic JSON correction before throwing an error. If your n8n version does not keep the toggle enabled after import, enable Auto-Fix Format manually in the node parameters.

nodes.name: Build Release Email Content
nodes.notes: AI success path. Builds the final HTML release email from the structured copywriter output and extracted release metadata. If AI output fails, the workflow uses the deterministic fallback node instead.

nodes.name: Build Fallback Release Email Content
nodes.notes: No-AI fallback. Builds the release email deterministically from extracted changelog data if the AI path fails.

nodes.name: Assemble Email Content
nodes.notes: Convergence point for AI-generated and fallback email content.

nodes.name: List All Subscribers
nodes.notes: Loads newsletter recipients. Add an active=true filter here if you implement unsubscribe handling.

nodes.name: Loop Over Subscribers Batch 10
nodes.notes: Processes recipients one at a time. The loop output sends each email; the done output routes to workflow completion.

nodes.name: Send Release Announcement Email
nodes.notes: SMTP delivery node. Replace the example sender and configure SMTP credentials before production use.

nodes.name: Wait for 1 Second
nodes.notes: Simple delivery throttle between recipients. Increase this delay if required by your SMTP provider.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ { "success": true, "message": "Notification sent", "version": $('Parse Release Versions From README').first().json.version_label, "versions": $('Parse Release Versions From README').first().json.versions, "recipients": $('List All Subscribers').all().length, "quality_gate": $('Assemble Email Content').first().json.quality_gate } }}

nodes.name: When Manually Started
nodes.notes: Manual production trigger. Edit "Configure Manual Send" first: version=<versions>, SEND_EMAIL=YES. Missing values fail before any email node.

nodes.name: Validate Release Send Parameters
nodes.notes: Safety gate. Stops execution before subscriber retrieval unless at least one semantic version is valid and SEND_EMAIL is exactly YES.

nodes.name: Set Webhook Release Parameters
nodes.notes: Webhook path: send JSON fields version, optional changelog, and SEND_EMAIL=YES. Empty or missing version, or missing SEND_EMAIL=YES, stops before any email node.

nodes.name: If Triggered by Webhook
nodes.notes: Routes completion by trigger type. Webhook executions must return an HTTP response; manual executions must not call Respond to Webhook.

nodes.name: Mark Manual Send Complete
nodes.notes: End of a successful manually triggered newsletter send.
